title.title: Goldfeld's conjecture: half the twists have rank 0
title.subtitle: Claim: among quadratic twists of any $E/\mathbb{Q}$, analytic ranks 0 and 1 each have density $1/2$

object.axisLabel: average analytic rank of the twists $E^{(d)}$

beats.text: Twist a curve $E$ by $d$: Goldfeld (1979) predicted average analytic rank exactly $1/2$
Before: only upper bounds, and only assuming GRH
The claim: rank 0 for half the twists, rank 1 for the other half

achievement.label: Goldfeld's conjecture (1979)
achievement.context: Before: Smith (2022) gave Selmer coranks 0 and 1 half the time each; the analytic side was missing
achievement.note: Twists by signed squarefree $d$ ordered by $|d|$, not fundamental discriminants

verify.detail: Not formalized; about 171 pages, and the BSD and H10 claims build on it
verify.ourCheck: We read the main theorem and caveats; nothing was checked independently

sources.quote: Goldfeld (1979) conjectured mean rank 1/2 in quadratic twist families.
Smith (arXiv:2207.05674, 2022) proved the 2-infinity Selmer corank is 0 or 1 with density 1/2 each for every E/Q
analytic rank 0 and analytic rank 1 each have density 1/2
Counts signed squarefree d ordered by |d|, slightly different from Goldfeld's fundamental discriminants
Not formalized; ~171 pages; feeds the BSD and H10 families
read each family's summary and abstracts and the introduction and main theorem of every principal paper

plain: Twist one elliptic curve every possible way: half the twists get rank 0, half rank 1, like a fair coin

steps: Smith: an algebraic rank is 0 or 1, half the time each
New: at the prime 2, that rank equals the analytic rank
So the analytic ranks split half and half too

voice.text: Twist a curve every way. Goldfeld predicted average rank one half. Before, only upper bounds.
Smith did the algebraic side. A new converse at the prime two transfers it.
Claimed: half rank zero, half rank one.
